newsitem.title: GERMANY: German printer wins rupee note contract - newspaper.
newsitem.headline: German printer wins rupee note contract - newspaper.

text.p: Germany's federal printing company, the Bundesdruckerei GmbH, has won a 130-million mark ($77.8 million) contract from India to print 3.6 billion rupee notes, the Frankfurter Allgemeine Zeitung newspaper said on Wednesday.
A spokesman for the federal printer in Berlin declined to comment on the story. "We will be able to say more next week," Hans-Joachim Schulz-Heisel said.

The newspaper article said the contract was the largest in the history of the printing company, which is 100 percent owned by the government and prints half of the German marks in circulation. It prints about 550 million banknotes each year.

The Bundesdruckerei, which has printed bank notes for Peru and Bolivia and other South American countries, beat several other bidders to print two billion 100 rupee notes and 1.6 billion 500 rupee notes, the paper said.
It won the contract by offering to do the job for $1.5 less per 1,000 notes than its closest rival, Canadian Banknote Company.
Rivals including Thomas de la Rue of London and Munich's Giesecke & Devrient, which prints the other half of the notes in Germany, were also outbid by the federal printer.
"The price miracle of Bombay was made possible because the Bundesdruckerei will subcontract the orders from India to printers in the Ukraine and in South Africa," the Frankfurter Allgemeine wrote.
